question: Which of the following geographical boundaries and territories of the Portuguese 'Estado da Índia' is NOT correctly matched?
options: Província do Norte (Northern Province) - Coastal strip including Daman, Diu, Bassein (Vasai), and Chaul
Capital of the Estado da Índia - Shifted from Cochin to Goa in 1530 under Governor Nuno da Cunha
Bassein (Vasai) - Ceded to the Portuguese by Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1534
Daman - Captured by the Portuguese from the Zamorin of Calicut in 1559
wrong_fact: Daman was captured from the Sultan of Gujarat (or local nobles under him), not from the Zamorin of Calicut.
explanation: Daman is located in western India (modern Gujarat/Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu). The Portuguese acquired it in 1559 from the nobles of the Sultanate of Gujarat to reinforce their control over the Gulf of Khambhat. The Zamorin was the ruler of Calicut in the far south (Malabar coast).

question: The Estado da Índia was not a continuous land empire but a network of ports. Which of the following spatial details regarding its territorial expansion is NOT correctly matched?
options: Nuno da Cunha (1529-1538) - Shifted the capital to Goa, acquired Bassein and Diu from Gujarat
Treaty of Bassein (1534) - Signed between Bahadur Shah of Gujarat and Nuno da Cunha, ceding Bassein and the island of Salsette
Fort of Diu (1535) - Constructed by the Portuguese with the permission of Bahadur Shah during his conflict with Mughal Emperor Humayun
San Thome de Mylapore - An administrative outpost on the Konkan coast established to oversee the spice route from Ceylon
wrong_fact: San Thome de Mylapore (modern Chennai) is located on the Coromandel coast (southeastern India), not the Konkan coast (western India).
explanation: San Thome de Mylapore was an important Portuguese settlement and trade node established on the southeastern Coromandel coast. It grew around the tomb of St. Thomas the Apostle. The Konkan coast is located on the western side of India, stretching from Mumbai to Goa.

question: At its territorial peak, the Estado da Índia stretched across the Indian Ocean basin. Which of the following geographic matches of its outer limits and dependencies is NOT correctly matched?
options: Macau - Established as a leasehold trading post in the Pearl River Delta of China in 1557
Nagasaki - Opened to Portuguese trade and temporarily ceded to the Jesuits in 1580 to secure the silk trade
Ormuz (Hormuz) - Lost to a joint Anglo-Persian force in 1622, marking the beginning of the decline of the Estado da Índia
Masulipatnam - The primary naval base of the Estado da Índia in the Bay of Bengal, protected by a large fortress built in 1520
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam was never a primary naval base of the Estado da Índia, nor did they build a large fortress there in 1520; it was a Golconda port where the Dutch, English, and French later established their major factories.
explanation: The Portuguese did trade at Masulipatnam but they never established a major military fortress or primary naval base there. In the Bay of Bengal, their main settlements and bases were at San Thome de Mylapore, Nagapattinam, and Hughli. Masulipatnam remained under the control of the Qutb Shahi (Golconda) rulers and later became a major site for English and Dutch commercial activities.
